correctness.rationale: The stated facets are precisely the open neighborhoods. A two-wing face with any allowed central-row vertex has a unique center even though the bare same-color diagonal has two; a one-wing face with two central-row vertices also has a unique center. In each matching, decreasing subset size removes every larger coface other than the paired one, and the stages leave exactly the four row boundaries, the four crown interfaces and the paired diagonal triangles. For the CW part one can move mixed-edge endpoints to basepoints inside each respective row sphere, up to homotopy of attachments; the row paths appearing in the triangle relations then contract because each sphere is simply connected. In this presentation the interface tree relations successively identify one new edge with the previously retained edge, by attaching a bigon with a free new edge before attaching the unused 2-cells. This justifies homotopy cancellation, not merely elimination in a chain matrix. The ordinary four-bridge graph is a circle, with 4(m²−3m+1) null-loop cells. Each opposite diagonal is eliminated using its first triangle; its second triangle goes once around that circle, not twice. One kills the circle integrally; the other 2m−1 attach trivially. The four row spheres retain their homotopy types. The sphere count is 4m²−10m+3 in dimension two plus four spheres in dimension m−2; at m=4 this is 31 two-spheres. The independent tuple-face replay in /workspace/review-evidence/replay.py (argument 3, output 3.txt) checks all strict cofaces for both collapse stages at widths 4–7, the diagonal incidences, and Euler characteristics 32, 50, 92 and 126. The all-width and integral conclusions follow from the proof, not the replay.

value.rationale: This computes an integral homotopy type at the first period where the long-cycle unique-center mechanism breaks, not just another finite Betti table. The shared diagonals explain both the disappearance of the fundamental circle and the explicit 2m−1 sphere correction, which constrain extensions to graphs with squares. No claim is made about such arbitrary extensions or equivariant types.
